chat.a: Net sales were ¥320M in week 33, −1.2% vs last year — flat on the surface. Bags are +17.8% and are offsetting denim, which is −18.4%.
Mostly the Mini Crossbody, which is +50.5% vs last year and added ¥8M. Over the last four weeks, 45% of its orders came from new customers.

The Mini Crossbody has 3.1 weeks of supply, under the 4-week floor. It sells about 1,738 units a week; the gap to an 8-week target is about 8,510 units, before any open orders or inbound stock, which this data doesn't hold.
They are the soft spot: −11.9% vs last year, while stores are +5.1% and online +0.6%.

chat.q: Whose orders are falling in department stores?
chat.a: Older customers', faster than the rest. Gen X and Boomer orders in department stores are −29.6% vs last year, while Gen Z orders there are +14.9%. Across the brand, Gen Z new customers are +33.7%.

insights.headline: A flat week held up by one bag — Mini Crossbody is +50.5% with 3.1 weeks of stock left, while denim and department stores drag.
insights.deck: Net sales were ¥320M, −1.2% vs LY, better than −2.4% over the prior four weeks. Denim & Pants is the biggest product drag at −2.7 pts, and department stores take −3.6 pts. Bags cover most of it at +2.9 pts, nearly all from the Mini Crossbody (+2.6 pts).
insights.why: Two drags, one engine. Denim is down in both families — Weekend Straight −17.2%, Wide-Leg Trouser −20.3% — and has been for weeks (−15.6% over the prior four). Department stores are −11.9%, worse than −8.9% before, while Stores grew +5.1%. The Mini Crossbody is speeding up: +50.5% against +40.5% over the prior four weeks.

actions.t: Size a Mini Crossbody reorder now.
actions.b: 3.1 weeks of cover against a 4-week floor, selling about 1,738 a week. The gap to an 8-week target is about 8,510 units — indicative: the buyer nets off open POs and inbound, and checks lead time and size mix, before raising the order.

actions.t: Plan denim to the trend, not to last year.
actions.b: Denim is −18.4% vs LY and −15.6% over the prior four weeks. Stock is still in range (7.6 and 8.4 weeks), so fix the next buy rather than mark down.

review.headline: Most friction this week is about time periods and definitions, not wrong numbers.
review.text: Buyers asked 121 questions. Only 1 answer had a number the checker flagged; the bigger theme is 6 questions where “October” or “last month” was read as the last 4 weeks. One theme needs a business definition before anyone can fix it.
